title: Stardew Valley
wiki_lead:
Stardew Valley is a 2016 farm life simulation video game developed by Eric "ConcernedApe" Barone. Players take the role of a character who inherits their deceased grandfather's dilapidated farm. The game is open-ended, with players managing the farm by clearing land, growing seasonal crops, and raising animals. Players can acquire skills in farming, foraging, fishing, mining, and combat. Social features include building relationships with townspeople, with the option to marry and have a child. A later update added multiplayer, allowing online play with others. 
Barone created Stardew Valley by himself over five years as an indie developer. He began the project to improve his programming and game design skills. He was heavily inspired by the Harvest Moon series (now named Story of Seasons), with additions to address some of those games' shortcomings. British studio Chucklefish approached Barone halfway through development with an offer to publish the game, allowing him to focus on completing it. It was released for Windows in February 2016 and was subsequently ported to other platforms, including home video game consoles, handheld consoles, mobile phones, and operating systems.
Stardew Valley received generally positive reviews from critics, including Yasuhiro Wada, the creator of Harvest Moon. The game has been cited as one of the best video games ever made and is credited with causing a resurgence in popularity for the farming sim genre. It became one of the best-selling video games, selling 50 million copies by February 2026. The game appeared on several publications' year-end lists and received accolades, including the Breakthrough Award at the Golden Joystick Awards and a nomination for Best Game at the British Academy Games Awards.

Gameplay

Stardew Valley is a farm life simulation video game set in top-down perspective. The open-ended game starts with the player character leaving their corporate job to manage a farm just outside of Pelican Town, located in the eponymous Stardew Valley. The farm inherited from their deceased grandfather must be restored, and players must assist in the town's revival.
Players may choose from several different farm types, each with a unique theme and different benefits and drawbacks. Each theme helps players focus on upgrading different types of skills faster. On the farm, players need to cut down trees, break rocks, and use a scythe to clear weeds to make space for tilling and planting. The farming system allows players to plant seasonal seeds that require daily watering and generally must be harvested before the next season. Players can also build barns and coops to raise animals for products like eggs and milk. As the game progresses through four 28-day seasons, players can complete certain tasks known as bundles. Players must collect a set amount of goods to complete each bundle and bring them to the Community Center to unlock new areas and activities such as a new island.

grok_lead:
Stardew Valley is an open-ended farming simulation role-playing video game in which players inherit an overgrown farm plot in a rural valley and restore it through activities such as crop cultivation, animal husbandry, resource gathering, crafting, combat in mines, fishing, foraging, and building relationships with townsfolk, including marriage and family-raising options. The game supports single-player and co-op multiplayer (1â8 players on PC via split-screen, LAN, or online; 1â4 players on consoles; online co-op on Nintendo Switch requires a Nintendo Switch Online subscription, while local split-screen or wireless co-op does not), with experimental co-op multiplayer available on mobile (Android and iOS, excluding Apple Arcade version) since the 1.6 update. The game was developed single-handedly by Eric Barone, known online as ConcernedApe, over approximately 4.5 years using self-taught skills in programming, art, music, and design, and self-published for Microsoft Windows on February 26, 2016, via Steam. Ports followed for Linux and macOS on July 29, 2016, PlayStation 4 and Xbox One in December 2016, Nintendo Switch on October 5, 2017, PlayStation Vita on May 22, 2018, iOS on October 24, 2018, and Android on March 14, 2019. A Nintendo Switch 2 Edition released on December 25, 2025. As of February 2026, Stardew Valley had sold over 50 million copies worldwide. By December 2024 it had sold over 41 million copies, with 26 million on PC and 7.9 million on Nintendo Switch alone, demonstrating its enduring commercial success driven by organic word-of-mouth, frequent free updates including the major 1.6 expansion released in March 2024 and subsequent patches up to version 1.6.15 on December 20, 2024, and appeal to players seeking relaxed, replayable gameplay amid fast-paced modern titles. It received critical acclaim for its depth, pixel art style, and Barone's comprehensive solo execution, earning nominations including BAFTA Games Awards and Game Developers Choice Awards. It faced no major controversies beyond typical indie development challenges like porting delays. Stardew Valley is rated E10+ (Everyone 10+) by the ESRB and 10+ by Common Sense Media. It is generally considered suitable for children aged 10 and up due to its relaxing farming simulation gameplay and positive themes of community building and personal growth. However, it includes mature elements such as alcohol use in a saloon, themes of depression and alcoholism in character backstories, mild fantasy violence (fighting monsters), simulated gambling, mild language, and implied romantic/sexual situations in relationships and marriage. Parental guidance is recommended for younger players due to these themes. ## Setting and Lore Stardew Valley is set in the rural Ferngill Republic, a nation engaged in an ongoing war with the neighboring Gotoro Empire. This conflict is subtly referenced through in-game dialogues, letters from relatives serving in the military, and character backstories (e.g., some villagers mention family members affected by the war or propaganda influences). It adds underlying tension to the otherwise peaceful valley, explaining certain absences, attitudes, or events without becoming a central plot driver.

An additional layer of ancient lore involves the Elemental Wars, a prolonged magical conflict lasting approximately 1,000 years between the Dwarves (a reclusive underground race) and the Shadow People (including the sewer-dwelling Krobus). Though the war has long ended, deep-seated resentment lingers between the two groups. This history surfaces in specific events, such as a confrontation in the Pelican Town sewers where the Dwarf and Krobus fight, only to be separated by the Wizard, who casts a "Seal of Promises" to enforce peace after both parties agree to end hostilities.

These background conflicts enrich the game's world-building, providing exciting narrative depth through hidden dialogues, artifacts, and rare events, while contrasting with the player's primary focus on farming, relationships, and exploration. They are optional discoveries that reward attentive players exploring beyond the surface-level cozy gameplay.
